html:
The Indus Waters Treaty is the 1960 agreement that divides the rivers of the Indus system between India and Pakistan. Jawaharlal Nehru and Ayub Khan signed it in Karachi after nine years of talks run by the World Bank.

The Partition of India in 1947 drew a border across the Punjab's canal network, the one built in the canal colonies, leaving the river heads in India and many of the fields in Pakistan. In 1948 India briefly cut the flow, which showed how fragile things were.

The treaty gave the three eastern rivers, the Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, to India, and the three western ones, the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, mostly to Pakistan. It paid for new dams and link canals in Pakistan, among them Mangla and Tarbela. It survived several wars and was long held up as a rare success between the two. In April 2025, after an attack in Kashmir, India said it was holding the treaty in abeyance.
sum: The Indus Waters Treaty is the 1960 agreement that divides the rivers of the Indus system between India and Pakistan. Jawaharlal Nehru and Ayub Khan signed it in Karachi after nine years of talks run by the World Bank.
